solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bunk with corner bath

parts.note: to corner something is to hog it, keeping it to yourself
a wash is a bath, as in having a wash

explanation.surface: A sleeping berth that comes with a bath tucked into the corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bunk' looks like a bed, but here it is nonsense; 'corner' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Bunk and hogwash are both informal words for nonsense or rubbish talk.

clue.text: Gets tango with energy — and speed

parts.note: to get something is to have it, so gets gives has
Tango is T in the NATO phonetic alphabet
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A dancer picks up the tango with vigour and pace.
explanation.definitionFit: Haste is hurried quickness, a synonym of speed.

clue.text: Good endorsement for pleasure

parts.note: ratification is formal approval or endorsement

explanation.surface: A good review or approval is given for the sake of enjoyment.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratification is the feeling of satisfaction or delight, a synonym of pleasure.

clue.text: Stop to maintain temperature

parts.note: to maintain a claim is to assert or aver it

explanation.surface: An instruction to halt so as to keep the heat steady.
explanation.definitionFit: To avert something is to prevent or ward it off, so to stop it happening.

clue.text: Meat for each picnic basket

parts.note: ham is a kind of meat
per means for each, as in a pound per person

explanation.surface: Sliced meat portioned out for each person's picnic basket.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamper is a large lidded wicker basket used for carrying picnic food.

clue.text: Papa's after fruit stout

indicators.note: after places the papa letter behind the fruit in the answer

parts.note: a plum is a fruit
Papa is P in the NATO phonetic alphabet; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: Dad has gone off in search of fruit, or is chasing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Plump and stout are both polite words for being rather fat.

clue.text: Critically review a hotel in church style

parts.note: to pan a show is to review it harshly

indicators.note: in puts the hotel letter inside the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A critic slating a hotel that has been done up in an ecclesiastical style.
explanation.definitionFit: Panache is flamboyant confidence and flair, a kind of stylishness.

clue.text: Somewhat dull university magazine is supported by one local

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath, so the local comes after

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a local is a native of a place

explanation.surface: A rather boring student magazine kept going by one person from the town.
explanation.definitionFit: Unimaginative means lacking creativity, so flat and uninspiring, a near synonym of dull.

clue.text: Producer initially embarrassed about number put on

indicators.note: initially asks for only the opening letter of Producer
about means the embarrassed word goes around the number

parts.note: someone embarrassed goes red
ten is a number

explanation.surface: A theatre producer, red-faced, fusses over a musical number being staged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' looks like staging a show, but it means feign.
explanation.definitionFit: To put on an accent or air is to fake it, which is to pretend.

clue.text: Conditions people in general appreciate, like the best politicians?

parts.note: states are conditions, as in a state of repair
man can mean humankind, people in general
to appreciate something is to like it

explanation.surface: A list of what voters want, praised as the mark of top politicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Statesmanlike describes the wise, dignified conduct expected of a great political leader; the question mark flags a definition by example.

clue.text: Letter pi in cast steel

indicators.note: metal that is cast is poured into a new shape, so these letters are remoulded

explanation.surface: The Greek letter pi moulded in steel, like a foundry's sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' suggests pi itself, but it is a written letter, as in St Paul's Epistles.
explanation.definitionFit: An epistle is a formal or literary letter, especially those in the New Testament.

clue.text: Bird in bamboo around river

indicators.note: around means the cane goes round the river letter

parts.note: a bamboo stem is a cane

explanation.surface: A wading bird stands among bamboo by the riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: The crane is a tall long-legged wading bird.

clue.text: Friend crossing border at an early stage

indicators.note: crossing means the friend stretches across, so around, the border

parts.note: pal is an informal word for friend
a rim is a border or edge

explanation.surface: A companion crossing a frontier at the start of a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Primal means primitive or original, belonging to the earliest stage of development.

clue.text: Swiss mountain climbing? Severe, wanting new cover for wound

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means the mountain word reads from the bottom up

parts.note: an alp is a mountain in Switzerland

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the new letter is dropped

parts.note: stern means severe

explanation.surface: A harsh Alpine climb leaves someone needing a dressing for a cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing?' turns ALP into PLA; 'wanting' takes N from STERN to leave STER.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaster is a sticking plaster, a small adhesive dressing put over a cut.

clue.text: A group of planes RAF sent up to show weapons

indicators.note: in a down clue sent up means the run is read upwards, so backwards
a group of the letters means a run taken from inside the words

explanation.surface: An air force squadron flown up for a display of firepower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A group of' takes LANESRA from 'planes RAF', and 'sent up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: An arsenal is a store or stock of weapons, so it stands for the weapons themselves.

clue.text: Following live female deer

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
a hind is a female deer

explanation.surface: Tracking a living doe through the woods.
explanation.definitionFit: Behind means at the back of or after, which is following.

clue.text: Good trick when trapping old game bird

indicators.note: trapping means the trick holds the old letter inside

parts.note: a ruse is a trick

explanation.surface: A clever ruse for snaring an elderly bird on a shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: The grouse is a plump bird shot for sport, hence a game bird.

clue.text: Gather admission of stupidity

definitions.meaning: read as two words, ... sounds like I am an ass: ..., a confession of being foolish

explanation.surface: Collecting together an acknowledgement of one's own foolishness.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as AM ASS: what you would say owning up to being foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to gather a large amount; AM ASS is a confession of being an idiot.

clue.text: Arrest in motion — time to begin again

indicators.note: in motion means moving about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A police arrest made on the move, and time to start over.
explanation.definitionFit: To restart is to start once more, a direct synonym of begin again.

clue.text: Mischievous child in small temporary accommodation

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a camp is a set of tents or huts for a short stay

explanation.surface: A naughty youngster at a little tent site.
explanation.definitionFit: A scamp is a playful rascal, usually a cheeky child.

clue.text: Tool to grip and lift weights, holding grams

indicators.note: holding means the weights word contains the grams letter

parts.note: tons are units of weight
G is the abbreviation for grams

explanation.surface: A gym implement for gripping and lifting weights, measured in grams.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongs are a two-armed implement used for picking up and holding things.

clue.text: What surveyors use out training shuffling around Los Angeles

indicators.note: around means the mixed letters surround the city's abbreviation
shuffling mixes up the order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Surveyors out on a training exercise, wandering round Los Angeles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'training' looks like the surveyors' exercise, but it is just fodder for 'shuffling', and 'around' wraps the result about the city's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Triangulation fixes positions by measuring angles from known points, the classic land-surveying method.

clue.text: Genuine about name of the kidneys

indicators.note: about means the genuine word goes around the name letter

parts.note: real means genuine

explanation.surface: A real story about the name given to the kidneys.
explanation.definitionFit: Renal is the medical adjective relating to the kidneys.

clue.text: Royal note returned by newspapers

indicators.note: returned means the note is turned back to front

parts.note: me (or mi) is the third note of the sol-fa scale
the press means newspapers collectively

explanation.surface: A royal's message bounced back by the papers.
explanation.definitionFit: An empress is a female emperor, a member of royalty.
